newsitem.title: USA: Colonial Pipeline distributary in south has leak.
newsitem.headline: Colonial Pipeline distributary in south has leak.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline Co repaired a leak on a Tennessee distributary of its huge distillate pipeline, and is restarting the line, Colonial officials said.
The Atlanta-based company said about 63,000 gallons (1,500 barrels) of distillates leaked out of failed weld seam in a rural area near Murfreesboro, Tennessee, the company said.
"We are in the process of starting it, but we are not up yet," said Colonial spokesman Sam Whitehead.
Whitehead said Colonial shut the the Chattanooga to Nashville, Tennessee distillate line Tuesday morning.

The weld seam failed during a previously-planned shutdown related to an upgrade of the line. Colonial was clearing the line of all of its product ahead of a switchover to a new section of line, but a failed valve caused pressure in the line to rise and provoked the rupture, Whitehead said.
Colonial delayed the switchover to the new line, he said.
Whitehead noted Colonial will be required by regulators to run the line at 80 percent of its 32,400 barrel per day (bpd) capacity pending further approval to run it at 100 percent.
The main Colonial distillate line moves about 960,000 (bpd) of distillates, including heating oil, diesel and jet fuel from Houston to Linden, New Jersey on the edge of New York Harbor.
Colonial also operates an adjacent artertial gasoline line that transports 1.2 million bpd from Refinery Row on the Gulf Coast to the populous Northeast.

Atlanta-based Colonial is a consortium of 10 companies including Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc unit, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaxo Inc, Unocal Corp's, Union Oil unit, and USX-Marathon Group's Marathon Oil Co.
